entries.answer: SpecSense AI is the featured project. For architecture depth, the SajiloGig and DeadManSwitch case studies are the best place to see how Aarya makes and explains technical trade-offs.

SpecSense AI checks software requirement specs and user stories for untestable terms like "fast" or "user-friendly" and suggests concrete, measurable replacements. It's built with Python, FastAPI, React, NLP, and Tailwind CSS.

questions: tell me about the inheritance project
entries.answer: DeadManSwitch is a decentralized digital inheritance tool. Files are encrypted in the browser with AES-256-GCM, the encrypted shards are stored on IPFS, and an on-chain heartbeat timer using ERC-4337 account abstraction releases access keys to a beneficiary if the owner stops checking in. No custodian is involved. It uses React, ethers.js, and the MetaMask SDK.

questions: tell me about the freelancing platform
entries.answer: SajiloGig is a student freelancing platform with role-based dashboards, visual ID verification, and a server-side escrow state machine. It's built with PHP, MySQL, and JavaScript.

questions: why not use smart contracts for escrow
why a state machine instead of Ethereum
why did you avoid blockchain in SajiloGig
entries.answer: For low-value micro-gigs, Ethereum gas fees ($5-$20 per transaction on mainnet) would cost more than the work is worth, so SajiloGig uses a server-side state machine (funded, working, submitted, approved) at no transaction cost. Photo KYC checks reduce throwaway client accounts, and auto-resolution timeouts stop disputed funds from getting stuck. The full write-up is in the Case Studies section.

questions: how do you store data on chain
how does DeadManSwitch keep costs down
is plaintext ever sent to a server
entries.answer: DeadManSwitch encrypts everything in the browser, so plaintext never touches a server. Only hashes are stored on-chain, since Ethereum storage costs about $0.64 per KB, and the encrypted data itself lives on IPFS.

SpecSense AI is Aarya's AI and NLP project: it parses requirement text to flag vague, untestable language and suggest measurable alternatives, built with Python and FastAPI. His other work is mostly full-stack, Web3, and QA.
